queued.headline: Queens Officers Revive Infant in Frantic CPR Rescue
queued.blurb: Two NYPD officers answering a call in Astoria performed CPR on a 1-month-old boy who was not breathing and had no pulse, saving his life.

queued.headline: Investigation Details Hourslong Ordeal for Six Nonverbal Students on School Bus
queued.blurb: Six students ages 6 to 8, all nonverbal with special needs, reached school more than four hours late after their bus went off route, an investigation found.

queued.headline: Brooklyn Conservatory of Music Opens Second Campus
queued.blurb: The Brooklyn Conservatory of Music has opened a second campus, NY1 reported.

queued.headline: Santos Bravos Marks First Anniversary at K-Pop Nara Ahead of NYC Debut
queued.blurb: Santos Bravos, billed as the voice of a new Latin generation, celebrated its first anniversary with fans at K-Pop Nara ahead of the group's New York debut.

queued.headline: New Charges Filed in FIT Student's Fentanyl Death
queued.blurb: Prosecutors brought new charges in the March fentanyl death of a Fashion Institute of Technology student, officials said.

queued.headline: Mamdani Asks Parking Lot and Garage Owners to Deny ICE Access
queued.blurb: Following the Oct. 8 Marble Hill shooting, the mayor asked private parking lot and garage operators to refuse access to immigration agents. Elected officials separately urged Target to stop ICE use of its Marble Hill lot.

queued.headline: Plaza Hotel to Close in January for Four-Year Renovation
queued.blurb: The Plaza's last day of service is set for Jan. 19, with renovation work starting the next day, according to a report.

queued.headline: Hochul and Blakeman Clash in Governor's Debate
queued.blurb: Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman sparred in a televised gubernatorial debate ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

queued.headline: Arturo O'Farrill Brings Afro Latin Jazz to Harlem
queued.blurb: Bandleader Arturo O'Farrill talked with NY1 about bringing his Afro Latin jazz to Harlem.

queued.headline: James and Komatireddy Trade Blows in Attorney General Debate
queued.blurb: Attorney General Letitia James called Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy a Trump puppet in a fiery NY1 debate and defended her remarks on the Cornell rape case.

queued.headline: Neir's Tavern Marks 197 Years With Free Block Party
queued.blurb: Woodhaven's Neir's Tavern, among the city's oldest bars, threw a free 197th anniversary block party on Oct. 3 with music, food and drinks.

queued.headline: Tokyo Record Bar Celebrates Thelonious Monk's 109th Birthday
queued.blurb: Tokyo Record Bar on MacDougal Street hosted a three-night tribute Oct. 8-10 for Thelonious Monk's 109th birthday, curated by his grandchildren Sierre Monk and Thelonious IV Monk.

queued.headline: Disco Tehran Celebrates Anniversary on Elsewhere Rooftop
queued.blurb: The Disco Tehran party marked its anniversary with a 4-10 p.m. rooftop session at Elsewhere on Sunday, Oct. 4.

queued.headline: Westside Cowboy Plays Music Hall of Williamsburg
queued.blurb: Westside Cowboy played Music Hall of Williamsburg on Tuesday, Oct. 6.

queued.headline: Bronx senior accused of shooting girlfriend, 70, and man, 60, then barricading himself
queued.blurb: An older man shot his 70-year-old girlfriend and a 60-year-old man in a Claremont building hallway, then barricaded himself, in what sources described as the end of an apparent love triangle.

queued.headline: New charges filed in FIT student's fentanyl death
queued.blurb: Prosecutors announced new charges in the March fentanyl death of a Fashion Institute of Technology student.

queued.headline: Sunset Park federal jail officer indicted in contraband bribery scheme
queued.blurb: A federal corrections officer at the Brooklyn jail in Sunset Park was indicted on charges of taking bribes to smuggle contraband.

queued.headline: Man found stabbed to death in Queens park
queued.blurb: A man was found stabbed to death in a Queens park, police said.
